challenges.question: For the upcoming 21-Dec Nainital→Crank's Ridge→Nainital geometry: what is the default transport mode under the train-first/1A rule, and when would an exception (local taxi/shared ride) be allowed? Cite the exact rule.
challenges.start_session_answer: The transport rule is not "train at all costs." governance/MARK_TRAVEL_PREFERENCES_CURRENT.md says: "train first when practical, especially useful overnight rail", "private car for mountains/last mile/door-to-door wins", and "Overnight train target: 1A / First AC; 2A only after Mark accepts fallback." governance/TRIP_FRAME_HARD.md restates: "Train first when practical", "Overnight rail target: 1A / First AC", "Private car for mountains / last mile / door-to-door wins", and "Door-to-door human burden controls." Therefore for a long intercity leg the default is train, with 1A as the overnight target. The 21-Dec Nainital-Crank's Ridge-Nainital problem is a local mountain/last-mile day geometry, so a private taxi/car is expressly allowed if rail is not practical and the whole-human door-to-door comparison favors road. A shared ride is not automatically preferred; it is acceptable only as a genuinely local mountain/last-mile access variant if it preserves the verified access, dwell, daylight and whole-human burden and is not being used as a disguised long-distance-bus fallback. Exact mode must still follow verified geometry/access.
